← FIBER FIELD LABDESIGN FOR REVIEW · 13 SEPTEMBER 2026
ENGINEERING + WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT

Automated trace intelligence.
Practical knowledge transfer.

A proposed production system and a working learning prototype for technicians with different experience levels.

Review status: No authorized AT&T documents were supplied. Every AT&T-dependent requirement is pending verification. This document does not assert AT&T compliance or authorize testing, repairs, live-fiber operations, or independent work.

1. Proposed system and scope

Use two connected workflows: collect and compare trace sets to identify evidence worth reviewing; turn approved, de-identified cases into short lessons that explain observations, uncertainty and the next justified action. Keep original measurements immutable and trace every automated finding to its source, rule version and reviewer.

Implemented now: a phone-oriented progressive web app with three learning paths, nine micro-lessons, six synthetic trace scenarios, immediate reasoning feedback, device-local practice progress, field references, and an offline learning cache. It has no instrument connection, real trace parser, live predictor, case-recording service or employer qualification integration.

Production assumptions: begin with conventional single-mode point-to-point fibers and an approved internal deployment. PON/splitter networks and other fiber types require separately validated acquisition and interpretation profiles. Vendors, fleet size, polling cadence, approved hosting, incident labels and retention requirements remain unknown. Numeric examples and pilot targets below are proposed design inputs, never AT&T acceptance limits.

2. Discovery questions, in priority order

  1. Which current AT&T documents govern optical safety, live-fiber tests, test setup, acceptance, escalation, data classification and qualification? Who owns each document and approves this use?
  2. Which instrument models, firmware, file variants, APIs, remote test systems and network access methods are authorized? Which fibers are active, dark, point-to-point or PON?
  3. How many fibers and traces per day are involved? Which directions, wavelengths, repeat counts and capture cadence are required?
  4. Are historical raw traces linked to trustworthy asset IDs, maintenance actions, repair outcomes and incident times? How many independently confirmed failures exist?
  5. Which mobile devices, browsers, internal hosting, identity systems, offline storage and training-record systems are permitted?
  6. How much paid training time can operations allocate? Which practical competencies and observed assessments authorize independent work?
  7. What warning horizon is operationally useful, what false-alert workload is sustainable, and which team owns each alert?

Proceed with synthetic learning and a vendor adapter contract while these are resolved. Do not schedule real tests or upload network information until the applicable requirements and authorization are established.

3. Architecture and end-to-end flow

Approved instruments / repositories→Collection adapters + scheduler→Durable queue→Raw store + metadata→Quality gate + event alignment→Rules / trends / validated models→Operations review→Reviewed case library→Mobile learning

Collection agents run within the approved network boundary with least-privilege instrument access. A scheduler requests measurements only through a verified vendor interface; otherwise an approved export watcher ingests completed files. The initial production deployment should be selected by the authorized architecture and security owners. On-premises processing keeps acquisition close to instruments; an approved cloud platform can scale batch analytics; a hybrid design transfers only authorized artifacts. None is presumed approved.

Separate immutable object storage for native traces from relational metadata and versioned features. A queue isolates unreliable collection from processing. Operators see overlays, matched events, quality exclusions, change histories, uncertainty, source files and the next required review. Alerts need deduplication by event and condition, persistence rules, maintenance suppression, severity, acknowledgment and escalation ownership. Missing data is its own condition, not a healthy result.

Use approved identity, role-based access, encryption, audit records, secret management and network segmentation. Separate technician learning access, analyst access and rule/policy publication rights. Record parser failures, collection delay, rejected comparisons, processing latency and alert volume. Define backup recovery objectives with owners and demonstrate restore/replay in a pilot. Do not place source credentials or production trace data in the learning PWA.

4. Trace-set definition and schema

A trace set is one acquisition session for a stable fiber asset, containing the prescribed matrix of direction × wavelength × pulse/setup profile × repeat. A historical series links compatible sets across time. A partial set remains visible but is marked incomplete. Match reverse-direction distances to the same physical event using verified fiber length and lead offsets.

EntityKey fields and relationships
Assetasset_id, route_id, endpoints, fiber type, expected length, topology, effective dates; one asset → many sets and incidents.
TraceSetset_id, asset_id, session_id, trigger, UTC timestamp, source timezone/offset, expected acquisition matrix, completeness, setup_profile_version.
Tracetrace_id, set_id, raw object reference, SHA-256, native format, direction, wavelength, pulse width, range, sample interval, averaging, refractive index, launch/receive lengths, device/firmware, calibration reference, acquisition timestamp, parser version, quality flags.
EventObservationobservation_id, trace_id, tracked_event_id, distance and uncertainty, loss, reflectance, slope, event width, local noise, dead-zone/saturation flags, extraction version. Raw observations survive later rematching.
TrackedEventtracked_event_id, asset_id, canonical distance, physical association when verified, valid-from/to, matching confidence. Splice replacement may create a new event identity.
Incident / maintenanceincident_id, asset_id, tracked_event_id when known, onset interval, discovery time, confirmed cause, evidence, repair action/time, certainty and reviewer. Avoid treating discovery time as exact failure onset.
Finding / predictionfinding_id, event or asset, source observations, baseline ID, target/horizon, rule/model version, score meaning, uncertainty, status, reviewer, acknowledgment and outcome.
Policy / case / lessonpolicy_id + version + scope + effective date + owner; case_id links redacted evidence and reviews; lesson_version links case, competency and governing policies. Retire affected lessons after policy changes.

Compare directly only when asset, event alignment and measurement conditions support it. Normalize distance offsets or resample onto a common axis with provenance; do not normalize away a physical loss. Different pulse widths, dead-zone masking, inadequate reach, unknown settings or changed topology can require exclusion instead. Store rejection reasons. Apply bidirectional averaging only to valid matched directional event losses under the governing method.

5. Collection and processing logic

for each authorized acquisition job:
    verify operational window, asset, device and approved setup profile
    request capture via verified adapter OR discover completed export
    transfer to staging; retry transient failures with bounded backoff
    validate completion and checksum; preserve original bytes
    deduplicate by source acquisition identity + content hash
    parse supported variant; quarantine malformed/unsupported files
    persist trace settings, timestamps and quality flags
    group into expected trace-set matrix; flag missing members
    if measurement quality insufficient: route for review; stop scoring
    select comparable baseline; align distance and matched events
    extract versioned features and uncertainties
    evaluate approved rules and persistence-aware trends
    if validated prediction model applies: score defined target/horizon
    record evidence, exclusions, versions and review status
    deduplicate/suppress/escalate finding under approved workflow
    after confirmed review: propose de-identified teaching case

Retries must not create duplicate remote captures after an uncertain response: reconcile the vendor job ID first. Retain source clocks and timezone information; flag uncertain alignment rather than silently correcting it. Use resumable transfers where supported, bounded retries and a dead-letter queue. Set retention and deletion controls only after policy verification. Firmware or parser changes trigger compatibility testing on retained golden files before production use.

6. Candidate event signatures

CandidateObservable evidenceConfounders / confirmationNext step
Connector conditionReflective event and possible loss change at a stable location.Peak shape alone cannot establish contamination; interface type, saturation and dead zones matter. Confirm through authorized inspection and repeat measurement.Follow approved connector verification workflow; preserve before/after evidence.
Splice degradationPersistent non-reflective event-loss change.Backscatter mismatch, bends and setup changes can resemble it. Match both directions and compare historical valid measurements.Review directional results and physical/maintenance context.
BendingLocalized loss with wavelength dependence, often greater at a longer single-mode wavelength.Fiber type, settings and other losses matter. A candidate signature is not a diagnosis.Confirm location and physical condition using the authorized method.
Distributed attenuationChanged slope across a span rather than one step.Wavelength, noise floor, fitting interval and unresolved events can change slope estimates.Verify comparable fitting regions and corroborate with required end-to-end tests.
Break or early endBackscatter ends before the expected endpoint; reflection may or may not occur.Range, poor reach, upstream loss or asset mismatch can mimic it.Verify expected length, setup and reverse direction where available; escalate.
Intermittent disturbanceEvent changes recur between comparable repeated captures.Connection handling, temperature, capture timing or acquisition noise; sparse sampling may miss events.Correlate timestamps and approved operational data; never infer absence between samples.
Apparent gainerNegative directional event loss with a corresponding reverse-direction difference.Different backscatter properties; not optical amplification. Match event before signed averaging.Use bidirectional interpretation under the required procedure.
Measurement artifactOverlapping peaks, saturation, ghost-like events or inadequate signal.Instrument/settings dependencies require original trace review.Flag measurement quality; retest under approved conditions before diagnosing fiber.

Confidence should distinguish measurement validity, event matching and causal interpretation. Do not combine them into an unexplained percentage. Event characteristics above are grounded in FOA’s OTDR reference; directional averaging is explained in EXFO’s gainer application note. These are general technical sources, not AT&T acceptance authorities.

7. Predictive quality: evidence and validation

Report four separate outputs: measurement validity; current conformance to a verified criterion; anomaly or trend strength; and, only when validated, failure probability within a named horizon. Initially use transparent change rules, robust baseline differences and persistence-aware trends. Maintain commissioning baselines and versioned post-maintenance baselines; do not silently absorb unresolved degradation into “normal.” Summarize event, fiber and route condition with visible coverage and unknown states, not a score that hides missing traces.

A proposed research target is a confirmed service-affecting fiber incident within seven days of a valid measurement. Operations must choose a useful horizon before labeling data. Use the incident onset interval and explicit confidence; traces after an incident or repair must not leak into pre-incident features. Assets without adequate subsequent observation are censored, not automatically negative. Route sharing, repeated traces and multiple alerts for the same incident require grouping.

Split training and evaluation by time and hold out related assets/routes. Compare models against no-skill, simple threshold and trend baselines. Report precision, recall, precision–recall AUC, false alerts per fiber-month, missed incidents, warning lead-time distribution and calibration with confidence intervals. Evaluate by instrument, fiber type, route and setup; disclose small samples. If labeled failures are insufficient, deploy reviewed anomaly detection only.

Monitor input changes, score distribution, false-alert workload and confirmed outcomes. Version datasets, feature code and models. Review drift and rule changes before release. Candidate retraining must beat the frozen baseline on an untouched later test set and pass owner review. Do not claim predictive accuracy from this app’s synthetic traces.

8. Policy traceability and review gates

Requirement areaAffected componentSource / version / statusProposed review role
Optical safety and live-fiber authorizationScheduler guards; handling lesson; job aidsPending AT&T verification — document not suppliedAuthorized safety and operations owners
Acquisition and acceptance limitsSetup profiles; comparison rules; decision lessonsPending AT&T verification — no limits configuredTest engineering and procedure owner
Data classification, hosting and retentionStores, exports, access, cache and auditPending AT&T verification — prototype contains synthetic data onlySecurity, privacy and records owners
Qualification and work authorizationCompetency progression and assessmentsPending AT&T verification — practice completion has no authorization effectTraining and operations owners
SME recording and case reuseCapture process, redaction, lesson approvalPending AT&T verification — no recording or real case submission enabledKnowledge owner and applicable policy reviewers
Alerts, repair and escalationFinding lifecycle and next-action contentPending AT&T verification — no production notifications enabledNetwork operations and procedure owner

The policy register must record exact document identity, version, effective date, applicability, owner, authorized source location and review date. A policy change creates an impact list of rules, profiles and lessons. Owners approve revisions, archive superseded versions and prevent expired content from being presented as current work guidance. Disagreements go to the designated procedure owner; an SME majority vote cannot override a mandatory procedure.

9. SME knowledge transfer with low time demands

Proposed cadence: one 10-minute case capture per participating SME per week, attached to an existing review window when practical; one 15-minute reviewer slot per week; and two 3–5 minute learner sessions per week. These are staffing proposals subject to approved work arrangements. Supervisors review pilot needs in a 10-minute weekly check rather than requiring daily reporting.

Use a short structured interview without recording unless recording is authorized: “What did you notice first? What else could cause it? Which next check separates the explanations? Which procedure applies?” A facilitator drafts the case so the SME only corrects the reasoning. De-identify traces and asset references before transfer to the learning system. Require independent technical review and policy review before publication.

Reusable case template

Case / revision: identifier, owner, competency, estimated lesson time.
Situation: de-identified context and expected task.
Evidence: trace-set references, settings, validity flags and annotated event.
Observe: directly visible characteristic.
Interpret: candidate explanation and alternatives.
Verify: measurement that would resolve uncertainty.
Act: source-linked approved next action and escalation condition.
Learning check: decision question, plausible distractors and explanation.
Governance: policy/version/scope, technical reviewer, policy reviewer, publication and expiry/review date.

10. Learning sequence and three sample micro-lessons

PathSequenceInitial practice time
Starting outSetup validity → event shape → handling and test interface10 minutes across three sessions
Building experienceFoundation plus wavelengths → pulse/detail → apparent gainer21 minutes across six sessions
Advanced / mentorAll prior lessons plus temporal change → early end ambiguity → explain a decision33 minutes across nine sessions

Each lesson teaches one decision using observe → interpret → verify → act and one retrieval question with explanatory feedback. Offer optional approved audio with captions in a later accessibility iteration; the current prototype uses readable text and labeled diagrams. Permit pause/resume, repeated practice and voluntary path selection. Never schedule notifications during driving or safety-sensitive work. Practical assessments must include uncertainty and appropriate escalation, not just correct labels.

  1. Wavelength relationship, 4 minutes: synthetic event at 2.5 km; 0.5 dB at 1310 nm and 2.4 dB at 1550 nm. Observe the greater loss, propose bending as one candidate, verify comparable conditions, then choose a source-authorized confirmation. Correct response: investigate; do not forecast a break.
  2. Directional relationship, 4 minutes: matched event −0.20 dB A→B and +0.50 dB B→A. Explain the backscatter effect and signed average of 0.15 dB. Correct response: no amplification and no pass/fail decision without governing limits.
  3. Temporal relationship, 5 minutes: valid comparable traces show increasing event loss. Ask whether that alone predicts failure tomorrow. Correct response: it supports investigation; a predictive claim requires an independently validated outcome model and warning horizon.

Proposed spaced practice: repeat one decision after two days and one week, within allocated training time. The prototype allows revisits but does not schedule reminders. Independence requires the employer’s approved qualification process and an observed practical assessment; completing these questions is not sufficient.

11. Pilot, acceptance criteria and roadmap

Phase 0 — governance and inventory: procedure owner verifies sources and scope; engineering verifies instrument contracts; security approves deployment/data boundaries. Exit when every production dependency has an owner and unresolved constraints are explicitly blocked from use.

Phase 1 — collection MVP: implement one verified vendor adapter and historical import, raw retention, metadata validation, event comparison and reviewer queue. Proposed acceptance: all supported golden files preserve hashes and required settings; malformed files are quarantined; repeated delivery creates no duplicate analysis; a replay produces traceable, reproducible results. Demonstrate safe recovery from interruption and failure to reach an instrument.

Phase 2 — learning pilot: provision a small authorized group across experience levels and review the first ten de-identified cases. Proposed usability targets: median lesson time no more than five minutes; at least 90% of participants can find the next learning activity without assistance; no critical content or accessibility defect. Compare pre/post and one-week unseen-case decisions, including correct escalation. Have training owners set competency thresholds before data collection. Do not equate time saved with safer performance.

Phase 3 — analytical shadow pilot: run rules and trends without automatic field actions; review alerts against confirmed outcomes. Before beginning, operations sets a tolerable false-alert budget and useful warning horizon. Report metrics and uncertainty rather than imposing invented universal values. A predictive release requires a pre-agreed improvement over simple baselines, useful lead time, calibrated probabilities and owner approval on an independent evaluation set.

Phase 4 — controlled scale: add validated vendors and fiber profiles, approved identity/training-record integration, drift monitoring, change control and restoration exercises. Roll back or disable a rule/model when its applicable conditions no longer hold. Estimate throughput after measuring actual trace sizes and parsing costs: daily raw bytes = fibers × sets/day × traces/set × mean trace size, plus retained versions and backups.

Measure repeat tests and rework by job complexity and exposure, alongside interpretation quality and procedural adherence. Avoid technician ranking from sparse practice results. Review aggregate workload and uncertainty rather than rewarding speed alone.

12. Example from measurement to reviewed learning

Three comparable synthetic sessions show one event rising from 0.40 to 0.62 to 0.84 dB. The quality gate passes, the event is matched and no intervening maintenance is recorded. A proposed persistence rule creates a review finding that includes the three source observations and the baseline. It reports “persistent loss increase; cause unconfirmed,” not a failure date.

The operator checks instrument conditions and authorized corroborating measurements, then follows the applicable procedure. If a cause is confirmed, the incident record captures evidence and repair timing. A redacted case explains what was observed, what alternatives were ruled out and why the next check was selected. Reviewers approve that case before it becomes a four-minute lesson. The confirmed outcome may later contribute to a separately governed predictive dataset.

13. Risks and mobile deployment limits

Main risks are inconsistent instrument exports, incorrect asset mapping, limited failure labels, artifacts mistaken for defects, noisy alerts, stale work guidance, and training that exceeds field time allowances. Mitigate with versioned adapters, explicit unknown states, independent review, measured workloads and policy-linked content.

The PWA includes a web manifest, phone icons and a service worker that caches only its own static synthetic learning assets. Practice state is device-local and can be cleared. There is no cross-device sync. A private hosted site requires sign-in online; offline cached content can remain on that device. Production use requires approved device/storage controls and a policy for expiry or removal of offline content. Do not use this cache design to distribute sensitive or changing operational instructions without those controls.

Installation and offline behavior depend on browser support, HTTPS, successful first caching and device policies. Physical iPhone and Android installation, airplane-mode relaunch and managed-device restrictions must be checked during the authorized pilot. The browser installation foundations are described in Google’s PWA course and service-worker documentation.
